checkpoints: During one editing burst, multiple edit(text) calls result in no immediate store write; after 120 ms without another edit, exactly the latest text is written.
A new edit before the quiet interval cancels and replaces the prior scheduled save.
After one burst saves, a later burst schedules and completes another save.
Opening or closing a view does not discard a pending document-buffer save merely because the current view badge or subscription changes.
A save-triggered synchronous navigation does not corrupt the buffer lifecycle or prevent later bursts from saving.
Public syntax/build checks remain valid, while recognizing that they do not establish business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not modify the adjacent search preview or its distinct quiet interval.
Do not continue writing to the store on every keystroke.
Do not change the public createWorkspace operations or the component's exposed coordinator API.
Do not transfer document-buffer ownership from the coordinator dictionary to the current view badge or its subscription.
Do not cancel a document's pending save solely because its view is closed, retired, or replaced.
Do not change source identities, text values, or status payload semantics.
Do not modify tests or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: A document buffer is identified by document id and owned by the coordinator dictionary.
The current view badge owns the live store subscription, not the document buffer.
Reopening the same document id must reuse the coordinator-owned buffer so it can accept subsequent save bursts.
The search preview has a separate transient trailing task and is not part of the document-buffer lifecycle.

obligations.text: Coordinator edit(text) must enqueue the text into the current document's existing trailing task instead of writing directly to the store.
The document trailing task must use a 120 ms quiet interval and write only the latest text received during that burst.
After a burst flushes, the same document buffer must remain reusable so subsequent bursts also save.
Pending document saves must persist independently of current-view retirement and subscription teardown because the coordinator dictionary owns the buffers.
Save execution must remain safe when synchronous store listeners navigate; task state must be retired before invoking the store-writing callback, as provided by the existing trailing utility.
Opening, editing, closing, disposing, document rendering, status subscription, and exposed public interfaces must otherwise retain their existing observable semantics.
The search preview implementation and its 40 ms transient quiet interval must remain unchanged.

ordering_barriers: For each edit burst: accept edit text, cancel any prior ticket for that document buffer, retain the newest text, then schedule a flush for 120 ms later.
No store write for the burst occurs before the trailing flush fires or is explicitly flushed.
On flush, the trailing task retires its ticket and saved value before calling the store-writing consumer, allowing synchronous callback reentry without leaving the task falsely active.
View retirement clears the current view and stops its subscription, but it must not retire the coordinator-owned document buffer.
A later burst begins only after or independently of the prior flush lifecycle and must be able to schedule a fresh ticket.
preservation: Preserve createWorkspace operations open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose().
Preserve initial document rendering from env.store.read(id) when a document is opened.
Preserve live status rendering for matching document events while that document's view subscription is active.
Preserve the behavior that edit does nothing when there is no current view.
Preserve synchronous store read, write, and subscription semantics.
Preserve coordinator-dictionary ownership of document buffers and view-badge ownership of only the live subscription.
Preserve all original source identities, text, and status payload meanings.
Preserve the search preview's existing query(text), hide(), and 40 ms trailing behavior.
scope: Business-code maintenance is limited to the workspace draft editor's document edit/save path, principally src/coordinator.js and its use of the existing trailing utility in src/services.js.
The Vue component remains a consumer of the coordinator API; no public component-interface change is required.
The adjacent search preview is explicitly outside scope.

edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
const resources=new Map(),bank={get(env,id){if(!resources.has(id))resources.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return resources.get(id);}};
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
